definitionEn: the study of human societies, cultures and how they develop
situation: Talking about the academic subject that studies how people live, their customs, beliefs and social groups.

examples.text: She studied [[anthropology]] and spent a year living with a fishing community in Indonesia.
Tech companies now hire experts in [[anthropology]] to understand how people really use their phones.
The museum's new [[anthropology]] gallery displays masks, tools and clothing from dozens of cultures.

texts: He took a course in [[anthropology]] to understand other cultures.
Her book combines history, [[anthropology]] and personal memories of the village.
Social [[anthropology]] looks at family, religion and power in different societies.

badCollocation.noteRu: Динозавров изучает palaeontology. Anthropology — наука о людях, их обществах и культуре.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Социальная антропология — social anthropology. Humanity — «человечество», astrology — «астрология», humanism — «гуманизм»; с social как название специальности они не работают.

nuance.text: For her [[anthropology]] project, she interviewed families about how they celebrate weddings today.
nuance.explanationRu: Anthropology изучает общества и культуры, в том числе современные, через наблюдение и интервью. Archaeology изучает прошлое по раскопкам и находкам, интервью о свадьбах — не её метод.

reverse.text: The [[archaeology]] team found Roman coins under the car park.
reverse.explanationRu: Раскопки и древние находки — это archaeology. Anthropology изучает людей и культуры, а не копает землю.

fixIt.text: She has a master's degree in social [[anthropologist]] from a university in Scotland.
fixIt.explanationRu: Anthropologist — это человек, специалист. Название науки и специальности — anthropology.

wordFormation.text: The research team spent a year doing [[anthropological]] fieldwork on a remote island.

definitionEn: to shock and upset someone very much because something is so bad
situation: Reacting to something so bad, cruel or shocking that you feel horrified and angry.

examples.text: Customers were [[appalled]] to discover that the company had sold their personal data.
I was [[appalled]] by the state of the hotel bathroom: mould on the walls and hair in the sink.
It [[appals]] me that some children still go to school hungry in such a rich country.

texts: Viewers were [[appalled]] by the way the contestants were treated.
Her parents were [[appalled]] when she left university to join a band.
Doctors are [[appalled]] at the long waiting times for surgery.

badCollocation.noteRu: Appalled — только о возмущении и ужасе. Если вид поразил красотой — amazed или stunned by the view.

collocationTask.prompt: I was ___ by the terrible conditions.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Прийти в ужас от чего-то — be appalled by. Appealed, applauded и appeased только похожи внешне: «обращаться», «аплодировать», «умиротворять».

nuance.text: We were [[appalled]] at how rudely the waiter spoke to the elderly couple.
nuance.explanationRu: Appal — вызывать ужас и возмущение чем-то недопустимым. Frighten — пугать, вызывать страх; грубость официанта возмущает, а не пугает.

reverse.text: The thunder [[frightened]] the children, so they hid under the table.
reverse.explanationRu: Испугать громом — frighten. Appal — возмутить чем-то плохим или жестоким, гром здесь ни при чём.

fixIt.text: Everyone was [[offended]] by the pictures of dead fish on the beach after the oil spill.
fixIt.explanationRu: Offended — «обиженный, задетый» лично. Ужас и возмущение от экологической катастрофы — appalled.

wordFormation.text: The service at the restaurant was [[appalling]]: we waited an hour for cold soup.

reply.context: Your friend says: "My landlord hasn't fixed the heating for three months, and it's January."
options: Oh, I'm appalled! What a lovely surprise for you.
One is appalled; kindly lodge a formal grievance with the relevant authority forthwith.
Three months? I'm appalled. You should report him to the council.
reply.explanationRu: Appalled — «в ужасе, возмущён», о приятных сюрпризах так не говорят. Второй ответ звучит как канцелярское письмо, а не поддержка друга.

definitionEn: a set of equipment or tools used for a particular scientific or technical job
senseNote: Здесь — «аппаратура, оборудование»; «государственный аппарат» (the state apparatus) — отдельное книжное значение.
situation: Talking about the special equipment used in laboratories, by firefighters, divers or in gym and science lessons.

examples.text: Firefighters wearing breathing [[apparatus]] searched the smoke-filled building for survivors.
Students must return all laboratory [[apparatus]] to the cupboard after the experiment.
The gymnasts warmed up on the floor before moving to the rings and other [[apparatus]].

texts: The divers checked their breathing [[apparatus]] before going under the ice.
Early photographers carried heavy [[apparatus]] up mountains to take a single picture.
The lab bought new [[apparatus]] for measuring air pollution.

badCollocation.noteRu: Фотоаппарат — a camera, телефонный аппарат — a phone. Apparatus — научное или техническое оборудование, а не бытовое устройство.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Apparatus — неисчисляемое, поэтому «один прибор» — a piece of apparatus. Device, instrument и appliance исчисляемые: a device, an instrument.

nuance.text: The researchers built special [[apparatus]] to measure tiny changes in temperature.
nuance.explanationRu: Apparatus — научное или техническое оборудование для особых задач. Appliance — бытовой электроприбор (холодильник, чайник); в лаборатории им ничего не измеряют.

reverse.text: Turn off every electrical [[appliance]] before you go on holiday.
reverse.explanationRu: Бытовые электроприборы — appliances. Apparatus — неисчисляемое слово для научного или технического оборудования.

fixIt.text: The chemistry teacher set up the [[aggregate]] for the experiment on the front bench.
fixIt.explanationRu: Aggregate — «совокупность, общая сумма», а не «агрегат». Лабораторное оборудование — apparatus.

definitionEn: attractive or interesting, so that you want to have or do it
senseNote: Здесь — «привлекательный, заманчивый»; appealing как форма глагола appeal (обжаловать, обращаться) — другое.
situation: Describing an idea, offer, place or design that attracts you and makes you want to try it.

examples.text: A four-day working week sounds [[appealing]], but it may not suit every business.
After a long winter, the idea of a week on a warm beach was very [[appealing]].
The designers made the packaging more [[appealing]] to younger buyers with bright colours and bold fonts.

texts: The job offer was [[appealing]], but the salary was too low.
Fresh herbs make any dish look more [[appealing]].
Living in the countryside has never been [[appealing]] to me.

badCollocation.noteRu: Привлекательный для кого-то — appealing to someone: The idea is appealing to me. Предлог for здесь звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Приятный на вид — visually appealing (или attractive). Attracting — форма глагола, а tasty и lovely с visually не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Lower fees make the online course more [[appealing]] than the classroom one.
nuance.explanationRu: Appealing — «заманчивый»: такой, что хочется выбрать. Charming — «обаятельный, очаровательный» о людях и местах; низкая цена курс обаятельным не делает.

fixIt.text: The idea of moving abroad seems very [[attracting]] to many young graduates.
fixIt.explanationRu: Attracting — форма глагола, в роли прилагательного «привлекательный» не работает. Нужно appealing.

wordFormation.text: The flat is small, but its location makes it very [[appealing]] to commuters.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Do you fancy a weekend hiking trip in the mountains next month?"
options: That sounds really appealing. I haven't had a proper break in ages.
Sounds appealing! I hate hiking and I'm terrified of heights.
Your proposal is deemed appealing and will be duly considered.
reply.explanationRu: Appealing — «заманчивый», так говорят о том, чего хочется. Во втором ответе слово противоречит остальному, а третий звучит как ответ комиссии, а не другу.

definitionEn: a strong wish or demand for a particular activity or experience
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «тяга, интерес, спрос» (an appetite for risk); буквальный аппетит к еде — базовое значение.
situation: Talking about how much people want something, such as risk, adventure, change, gossip or new products.

examples.text: Young investors often have a bigger [[appetite]] for risk than people close to retirement.
The public's [[appetite]] for celebrity gossip seems impossible to satisfy.
After two elections in one year, voters have little [[appetite]] for another campaign.

texts: Travelling as a teenager gave her an [[appetite]] for adventure.
There is a growing [[appetite]] for plant-based food in supermarkets.
The board showed no [[appetite]] for another expensive merger.

badCollocation.noteRu: Тяга к чему-то — appetite for something: an appetite for risk. Предлог to здесь — калька с русского «к».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тяга к приключениям — an appetite for adventure. Appeal for — «призыв», apathy — «безразличие», а addiction требует предлога to.

nuance.text: Teenagers have a huge [[appetite]] for short, funny videos.
nuance.explanationRu: У людей есть appetite for something — тяга к чему-то. Appeal — привлекательность самой вещи: short videos have huge appeal for teenagers, а не наоборот.

reverse.text: The film's [[appeal]] lies in its gentle humour.
reverse.explanationRu: Привлекательность фильма — its appeal. Appetite бывает у людей (тяга к чему-то), а не у фильма.

fixIt.text: After the crash, investors lost their [[wish]] for risky technology shares.
fixIt.explanationRu: Wish — «пожелание, мечта», с «потерять интерес к акциям» не сочетается. О готовности рисковать говорят appetite for risk.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "Management wants to relaunch the app next month. Will the team be up for it?"
options: Sure, the team's appetite is fine. They all had a big lunch today.
Honestly, after the last chaotic launch, there's not much appetite for another rush job.
The team's appetite for said relaunch shall be ascertained in due course.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь appetite — «желание, готовность» что-то делать, а не аппетит к еде. Третий ответ звучит как бюрократический отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

definitionEn: to publicly praise a decision, effort or quality you approve of
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «одобрять, приветствовать» (applaud a decision); «аплодировать, хлопать» — базовое значение.
situation: Saying publicly that you strongly approve of someone's decision, courage or effort, without actually clapping.

examples.text: I [[applaud]] your decision to tell the client the truth, even though it cost us the contract.
Environmental groups [[applauded]] the city's plan to ban cars from the centre, calling it long overdue.
Teachers should be [[applauded]] for keeping schools running during the floods.

texts: We [[applaud]] the council for finally fixing the roads.
Critics were quick to [[applaud]] the director's brave choice of ending.
I [[applaud]] anyone who learns a new language after sixty.

badCollocation.noteRu: Applaud — переходный глагол без предлога: applaud the singer, applaud her decision. Applaud to — калька с «аплодировать кому».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Похвалить кого-то за смелость — applaud someone for their courage. Clap — буквально «хлопать», approve требует of, а welcome — «приветствовать» гостя или новость.

nuance.text: Human rights groups [[applauded]] the court's decision.
nuance.explanationRu: Applaud может значить «одобрить, похвалить» без всяких хлопков. Clap — только буквально хлопать в ладоши, clap a decision не говорят.

reverse.text: The children [[clapped]] along to the music.
reverse.explanationRu: Хлопать в такт музыке — clap along. Applaud — аплодировать выступлению или одобрять решение, в такт так не хлопают.

fixIt.text: We [[applause]] your courage in speaking out about the problem.
fixIt.explanationRu: Applause — существительное («аплодисменты»). Нужен глагол: we applaud your courage.

wordFormation.text: The decision to cut ticket prices drew [[applause]] from fans and players alike.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I've finally told the boss I won't answer work emails at weekends any more."
options: Great! I'll come and applaud you every Saturday while you answer them.
Your assertiveness is hereby applauded by the undersigned.
Good for you! I applaud you for standing up for yourself.
reply.explanationRu: Applaud someone for something — похвалить, одобрить поступок. Первый ответ противоречит ситуации, а второй звучит как официальная грамота, а не реплика коллеги.

definitionEn: a machine used in the home, such as a fridge or washing machine
situation: Talking about fridges, cookers, dishwashers, kettles and other electrical machines people use at home.

examples.text: Old kitchen [[appliances]] like fridges and freezers can use a surprising amount of electricity.
The shop sells washing machines, cookers and other household [[appliances]] at discount prices.
Never use an electrical [[appliance]] with a damaged cable, as it could start a fire.

texts: Energy-efficient [[appliances]] cost more but save money over time.
The flat comes fully furnished, with all [[appliances]] included.
Our electricity bill dropped after we replaced two old [[appliances]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Приложение для телефона — an app (или application). Appliance — бытовой прибор: холодильник, чайник, пылесос.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Кухонная техника — kitchen appliances. Mechanisms — «механизмы», aggregates — не «агрегаты», а apparatus — научное оборудование.

nuance.text: Large kitchen [[appliances]], like fridges and cookers, are usually delivered free of charge.
nuance.explanationRu: Appliance — бытовой прибор для домашней работы: холодильник, плита, стиральная машина. Device — любое устройство, чаще небольшое и электронное; большие кухонные машины так обычно не называют.

reverse.text: Please switch off all electronic [[devices]], including phones and tablets, during the exam.
reverse.explanationRu: Телефоны и планшеты — electronic devices. Appliances — бытовые приборы вроде холодильника, а не гаджеты.

fixIt.text: We bought all our kitchen [[technics]] from one shop to get a bigger discount.
fixIt.explanationRu: Technics — не «бытовая техника». Холодильники, плиты и чайники — kitchen appliances.

definitionEn: relevant to or officially affecting a particular person, group or situation
situation: Saying whether a rule, law, fee or question is relevant to a particular person or case.

examples.text: If a question on the form is not [[applicable]] to you, simply write N/A.
The new dress code is [[applicable]] to all staff, including senior managers.
The findings of this small study may not be [[applicable]] to older patients.

texts: Delivery charges are [[applicable]] only to orders under thirty euros.
This discount is not [[applicable]] during the summer sale.
Her advice is [[applicable]] to almost any job interview.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Подходящий для работы» (о кандидате) — suitable for the job. Applicable — о правилах и законах: применимый, относящийся к кому-то.

collocationTask.explanationRu: В анкетах пишут delete (или tick) where applicable — «где применимо». Applicant — «кандидат», application — «заявление», applied — форма глагола.

nuance.text: The rules on overtime are not [[applicable]] to part-time staff.
nuance.explanationRu: Applicable to — «распространяется на кого-то» (о правилах, законах, тарифах). Suitable — «подходящий, годный» для цели или человека; о действии правил так не говорят.

reverse.text: This film is not [[suitable]] for young children.
reverse.explanationRu: «Не подходит для детей» — not suitable for children. Applicable говорит о том, на кого распространяется правило, а не о том, что кому подходит.

fixIt.text: The new safety rules are [[usable]] to all visitors, not just employees.
fixIt.explanationRu: Usable — «пригодный для использования» о вещах. Правила, которые распространяются на кого-то, — applicable to them.

wordFormation.text: Critics questioned the [[applicability]] of the study to real classrooms.

rewrite.original: These rules do not concern people who work part-time.
rewrite.frame: These rules are not ____ part-time workers.

definitionEn: to officially choose someone for a job or position of responsibility
situation: Talking about a company, government or committee officially giving someone a job, title or role.

examples.text: The board has [[appointed]] a new chief executive after months of searching.
She was [[appointed]] as the country's first female ambassador to Japan.
The school [[appoints]] two older students each year to represent pupils at staff meetings.

texts: The club [[appointed]] a former player as head coach.
A judge was [[appointed]] to lead the investigation.
She has just been [[appointed]] head of marketing.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Назначить встречу» — arrange или schedule a meeting. Appoint — назначать человека на должность.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ someone as head of the department
collocationTask.explanationRu: Назначить кого-то руководителем — appoint someone as head. Set, put и place значат «поставить» предмет; о должности так не говорят.

nuance.text: Judges in this country are [[appointed]] by the president, not chosen by voters.
nuance.explanationRu: Appoint — назначить: решение принимает руководитель или комиссия. Elect — выбрать голосованием; президент судей не «избирает», а назначает.

reverse.text: The town [[elected]] a new mayor with sixty per cent of the vote.
reverse.explanationRu: Если было голосование — elect. При назначении голосов и процентов нет, поэтому appointed здесь не подходит.

fixIt.text: The company has [[nominated]] a new finance director, who starts work in May.
fixIt.explanationRu: Nominate — выдвинуть кандидатом, а не назначить. Если человек уже получил должность и выходит на работу, нужно appointed.

wordFormation.text: The [[appointment]] of a new head teacher was announced this morning.

reply.context: A friend asks: "I heard your department finally has a new boss?"
options: Yes, and we appointed a meeting with her for Tuesday at ten.
Yes, they've appointed someone from outside the company. She starts on Monday.
Indeed, an appointment has been effected with regard to the vacant managerial position.
reply.explanationRu: Appoint — назначить на должность. «Назначить встречу» — arrange a meeting, а не appoint. Третий ответ звучит как приказ отдела кадров, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: They made her the new team leader last week.
rewrite.frame: She ____ the new team leader last week.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: she was appointed (as) team leader.
